research_question: Does offshore RMB price discovery accumulated while A shares are closed add China-specific information beyond the validated U.S. closure-accrual feature for the next CSI1000 opening gap?

financial_preanalysis.why_CNH: USD/CNH is an offshore RMB market that can continue repricing China-specific macro, policy and risk information while mainland A shares are closed. Compared with broad U.S. equity risk, it is economically closer to China-specific price discovery.
financial_preanalysis.expected_sign: A rise in USD/CNH means offshore RMB depreciation and is expected, all else equal, to be associated with a weaker China reopening gap; sign is diagnostic, not a selection gate.
financial_preanalysis.why_daily_is_causal: Only Yahoo Finance daily bars whose bar date is strictly earlier than the target China trading date are used. This conservative date rule excludes the target-date FX daily close, which may occur after the China open.
financial_preanalysis.why_closure_extra: As in v3, cumulative return minus the final daily return isolates information accumulated before the last daily bar; it is exactly zero when zero or one new observed daily intervals arrive between China information boundaries.

external_data_contract.adjustment: use unadjusted chart close; no interpolation or forward fill

time_boundary.start_level: latest observed CNH daily close with bar date strictly before previous China trading date
time_boundary.end_level: latest observed CNH daily close with bar date strictly before target China trading date
time_boundary.last_daily_return: end close / immediately prior observed CNH daily close - 1

attempts.features: frozen baseline plus v3 us_nasdaq_closure_extra and us_vix_closure_extra

primary_adjudication.mechanism_subset: rows with more than one CNH observed interval between China boundaries
primary_adjudication.progression_rule: V4 may progress only if full-holdout IC exceeds V3 comparator, full-holdout SSE is lower, and SSE improves on the multiple-CNH-interval mechanism subset. No PnL/Sharpe selection.
